ideas: Saving money and time through planning
Avoiding stress with a clear schedule
The fun of surprises on spontaneous trips

phrases.meaning: a feeling of calm, no worry
keep space or time for something

model: Personally, I prefer planned trips, although I like to leave room for a few surprises. First, planning saves money and time. When you book in advance, flights and hotels are usually much cheaper. For example, last summer my friends and I went to Phu Quoc on a whim during a public holiday. First, we found that most of the cheap hotels were sold out, and then we ended up paying almost double for a small room. We also wasted time every morning deciding what to do. Another reason is that a plan gives me peace of mind. I only get a few weeks of annual leave, so I want to make the most of every day. Last year, when I was travelling in Japan, I had a rough itinerary for each city, so I never had to worry about trains or tickets, and I could actually relax. I know spontaneous trips can be exciting, but for me, a bit of planning makes a holiday more enjoyable. So overall, I'd choose a planned trip.
